page: Amazon Web Services c8in.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated x86_64 Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The instance configuration provides 48 physical processor cores and 96 virtual cores through multithreading, along with 192.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 2.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio.

Network throughput is a central architectural feature of the c8in.24xlarge, offering a baseline networking bandwidth of 150 Gbps. The instance contains no integrated local storage and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes or network-attached storage for persistent operational data. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not included.

From a resource allocation standpoint, the system delivers high processing density and substantial networking capacity for compute-bound systems that require low network latency and high packet delivery rates. Tradeoffs involve strict reliance on external network volumes for storage access and a lean memory-to-core allocation. Best-fit workloads include distributed high-performance computing, network virtualization functions, continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, and compute-intensive backend application serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c8in.24xlarge is a high-bandwidth compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an x86_64 Intel processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. It is provisioned with 48 dedicated physical cores, 96 vCPUs, and 192.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Networking throughput reaches a baseline rate of 150 Gbps, tailored for data-heavy transport layers. The instance lacks local storage drives and hardware GPUs, meaning persistent file operations rely entirely on remote network block storage. Given its high core density, extensive network bandwidth, and compute-oriented memory ratio, the c8in.24xlarge fits parallel batch computation, network packet inspection appliances, distributed application nodes, and large-scale compilation tasks.
